story: Mama Rosa came to Texas from Monterrey with two suitcases and me on her hip. She cleaned offices at night and went to English classes in the mornings. She made tamales every Christmas Eve and the whole block would come by. She sang along to the radio in the car with all the windows down. When I got my first job she cried in the parking lot. She keeps every birthday card I ever made her in a shoebox under her bed. She taught me that a closed fist can't receive anything. She never missed one of my soccer games, even when she worked double shifts. She still calls me "mi cielo". She grows roses in coffee cans on the porch. Her laugh fills the whole house. She learned to drive at 45 and passed on the first try. She tells everyone that I'm her proudest work. She makes the best hot chocolate with cinnamon.
